\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਵਾਅਦਾ} (vāadā)}{ਵਾਅਦਾ (vāadā)}]{\pa{ਵਾਅਦਾ} (vāadā) — a promise}

\label{lesson:PA-C340-vaada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for by no means, then the Punjabi for to dig one's heels in.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਵਾਅਦਾ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਵਾਅਦਾ}} — \emph{vāadā} — \textquotedblleft{}a promise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਕੀ} \pa{ਤੁਸੀਂ} \pa{ਵਾਅਦਾ} \pa{ਕਰਦੇ} \pa{ਹੋ}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kī tusī̃ vāadā karde ho?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Do you promise?
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਵਾਅਦਾ}} (\emph{vāadā}) is a loan, usually traced through Persian to Arabic \emph{waʿda}, \textquotedblleft{}promise\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for asking and answering.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vāadā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vāadā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kī tusī̃ vāadā karde ho?} — Do you promise?
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Punjabi for by no means, then the Punjabi for to dig one's heels in, then say \emph{vāadā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \pa{ਵਾਅਦਾ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A promise\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਮਨਾਉਣਾ} (manāuṇā)}{ਮਨਾਉਣਾ (manāuṇā)}]{\pa{ਮਨਾਉਣਾ} (manāuṇā) — to persuade; to talk round}

\label{lesson:PA-C340-manauna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for to dig one's heels in, then the Punjabi for a promise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਮਨਾਉਣਾ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਮਨਾਉਣਾ}} — \emph{manāuṇā} — \textquotedblleft{}to persuade; to talk round\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਕੀ} \pa{ਅਮਨ} \pa{ਪਿਤਾ} \pa{ਨੂੰ} \pa{ਮਨਾਵੇਗਾ}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kī Aman pitā nū̃ manāvegā?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Will Aman talk his father round?
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \pa{ਮੈਂ} \pa{ਭੈਣ} \pa{ਨੂੰ} \pa{ਮਨਾਇਆ}, \emph{maiṁ bhaiṇ nū̃ manāiā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਮਨਾਉਣਾ}} (\emph{manāuṇā}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{manyate}, \textquotedblleft{}thinks, thinks fit, agrees\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Punjabi \emph{manāuṇā}, \textquotedblleft{}to persuade, soothe\textquotedblright{}, under it (CDIAL 9857).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for asking and answering.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{manāuṇā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{manāuṇā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kī Aman pitā nū̃ manāvegā?} — Will Aman talk his father round?
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Punjabi for to dig one's heels in, then the Punjabi for a promise, then say \emph{manāuṇā} again
  \item \emph{Write it:} copy \textbf{\pa{ਮਨਾਉਣਾ}} once, checking the whole word
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \pa{ਮਨਾਉਣਾ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To persuade; to talk round\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਬਿਲਕੁਲ} (bilkul)}{ਬਿਲਕੁਲ (bilkul)}]{\pa{ਬਿਲਕੁਲ} (bilkul) — absolutely; completely}

\label{lesson:PA-C340-bilkul}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for a promise, then the Punjabi for to persuade.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਬਿਲਕੁਲ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਬਿਲਕੁਲ}} — \emph{bilkul} — \textquotedblleft{}absolutely; completely\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਕੀ} \pa{ਤੁਸੀਂ} \pa{ਬਿਲਕੁਲ} \pa{ਤਿਆਰ} \pa{ਹੋ}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kī tusī̃ bilkul tiār ho?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Are you completely ready?
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਬਿਲਕੁਲ}} (\emph{bilkul}) is a loan, usually traced through Persian to Arabic \emph{bil-kull}, \textquotedblleft{}with the whole\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for asking and answering.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bilkul}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bilkul}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kī tusī̃ bilkul tiār ho?} — Are you completely ready?
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Punjabi for a promise, then the Punjabi for to persuade, then say \emph{bilkul} again
  \item \emph{Write it:} copy \textbf{\pa{ਬਿਲਕੁਲ}} once, checking the whole word
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \pa{ਬਿਲਕੁਲ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Absolutely; completely\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਕਬੂਲਣਾ} (kabūlṇā)}{ਕਬੂਲਣਾ (kabūlṇā)}]{\pa{ਕਬੂਲਣਾ} (kabūlṇā) — to accept; to admit}

\label{lesson:PA-C340-kabulna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for to persuade, then the Punjabi for absolutely.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਕਬੂਲਣਾ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਕਬੂਲਣਾ}} — \emph{kabūlṇā} — \textquotedblleft{}to accept; to admit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਕੀ} \pa{ਤੁਸੀਂ} \pa{ਮੇਰੀ} \pa{ਬੇਨਤੀ} \pa{ਕਬੂਲਦੇ} \pa{ਹੋ}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kī tusī̃ merī bentī kabūlde ho?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Do you accept my request?
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \pa{ਮੈਂ} \pa{ਉਸ} \pa{ਦੀ} \pa{ਬੇਨਤੀ} \pa{ਕਬੂਲੀ}, \emph{maiṁ us dī bentī kabūlī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਕਬੂਲਣਾ}} (\emph{kabūlṇā}) is a verb made in Punjabi from a loan, usually traced through Persian to Arabic \emph{qabūl}, \textquotedblleft{}acceptance\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for asking and answering.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kabūlṇā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kabūlṇā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kī tusī̃ merī bentī kabūlde ho?} — Do you accept my request?
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Punjabi for to persuade, then the Punjabi for absolutely, then say \emph{kabūlṇā} again
  \item \emph{Write it:} copy \textbf{\pa{ਕਬੂਲਣਾ}} once, checking the whole word
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \pa{ਕਬੂਲਣਾ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To accept; to admit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਸਮਝੌਤਾ} (samjhautā)}{ਸਮਝੌਤਾ (samjhautā)}]{\pa{ਸਮਝੌਤਾ} (samjhautā) — a compromise; an agreement}

\label{lesson:PA-C340-samjhauta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for absolutely, then the Punjabi for to admit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਸਮਝੌਤਾ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਸਮਝੌਤਾ}} — \emph{samjhautā} — \textquotedblleft{}a compromise; an agreement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਕੀ} \pa{ਤੁਸੀਂ} \pa{ਸਮਝੌਤਾ} \pa{ਕਰੋਗੇ}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kī tusī̃ samjhautā karoge?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Will you agree to a compromise?
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਸਮਝੌਤਾ}} (\emph{samjhautā}) is built on \emph{samajhṇā}, \textquotedblleft{}to understand\textquotedblright{}, which goes back to Sanskrit \emph{saṁbudhyate}, \textquotedblleft{}wakes up, understands\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Punjabi \emph{samajhṇā} under it (CDIAL 12959), but not \emph{samjhautā} itself.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for asking and answering.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{samjhautā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{samjhautā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kī tusī̃ samjhautā karoge?} — Will you agree to a compromise?
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Punjabi for absolutely, then the Punjabi for to admit, then say \emph{samjhautā} again
  \item \emph{Write it:} copy \textbf{\pa{ਸਮਝੌਤਾ}} once, checking the whole word
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \pa{ਸਮਝੌਤਾ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A compromise; an agreement\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
